There is therefore no GML source shape analogous to `timeline_index` to rewrite for `GmlSequenceState` — `entity.add(GmlSequenceState, {...})` remains real and exercised directly by tests, but wiring a real GML source pattern to it is not a transpiler rewrite this pass could honestly invent; it would need a real design decision about which entity a room-layer sequence instance corresponds to, which is a genuine, separate, not-yet-started follow-up.

### GMS2 rendering built-ins: `sprite_index` / `image_*` / `depth` transpile onto real `Sprite`/`Transform` fields

Found by reading a real generated `.behavior.ts` file end to end, not assumed: `sprite_index = spr_foo;` — GameMaker's extremely common per-instance sprite-swap idiom (idle/walk/attack/hurt state machines) — was falling through to `gms2-transpile.ts`'s generic "auto-declare on first bare assignment" pass. That pass only protects the _assignment target_ from throwing; it does nothing for a bare identifier used as a _value_, so `spr_foo` on the right-hand side stayed a genuinely undeclared identifier and threw `ReferenceError` the moment the generated function actually ran. Since a sprite-swap state machine touches at least `sprite_index` in nearly every real GameMaker object, this was a near-universal runtime crash on first play, not an edge case.

`gms2-transpile.ts` now rewrites seven real per-instance rendering built-ins for real, all targeting fields this engine's `Sprite`/`Transform` components already have (`components/Sprite.ts`/`components/Transform.ts`) — confirmed against `RenderPipeline._syncOne()`, which is what actually reads each of these onto the rendered PixiJS sprite every frame:

- **`sprite_index`** → `Sprite.texturePath`. A bare identifier (the common real shape, `sprite_index = spr_dad_hug;`) is quoted into this importer's own real texture-path convention, `./assets/sprites/<name>/frame_0.png` — the exact one `gms2-codegen.ts`'s `buildObjectPrefabJSON`/`buildSpriteAsset` already use for an object's own initial `spriteId`, so a `sprite_index` assignment and that initial sprite can never disagree on what a sprite's texture path is. GameMaker's own documented sentinel, `sprite_index = -1` ("remove the sprite from an instance"), resolves to `""` — `Sprite.texturePath`'s own default, already meaning "no texture" everywhere else in this engine. An equality comparison against a bare sprite-asset identifier on either side (`if (sprite_index == spr_dad_idle)`, the other extremely common real shape) is resolved the same way, before the generic bare-read rewrite runs — otherwise the identifier on the comparison's other side would be left unresolved and crash exactly the way the write side used to. A bare read of `sprite_index` itself becomes a safe `_entity.get(GmlActions.Sprite)?.texturePath ?? ""`. Anything that isn't a bare identifier or `-1` (a variable, another instance's `sprite_index`, a ternary) is assumed to already evaluate to a real texture-path string and passed through unchanged — this importer has no way to resolve an arbitrary runtime expression to an asset name ahead of time and doesn't pretend to.
- **`image_angle`** → `Transform.rotation` (not `Sprite`, which has no rotation field of its own — `RenderPipeline` reads `pixiSprite.rotation` from `Transform.rotation`). GameMaker's own value is degrees; this engine's is radians (matching pixi's convention), converted both ways with the exact `* Math.PI / 180` / `* 180 / Math.PI` factor `gmlCamera.ts`/`gmlProjection.ts` already use for every other GML-degrees-to-engine-radians field.
- **`image_xscale`/`image_yscale`** → `Transform.scaleX`/`.scaleY` (same reasoning as `image_angle` — `Sprite` has no scale fields). No unit conversion; both default to `1` on both sides.
- **`image_alpha`** → `Sprite.alpha`. No conversion; both default to `1`.
- **`image_blend`** → `Sprite.tint`, reusing the exact `0xBBGGRR`→`0xRRGGBB` conversion `compat/gmlActions.ts`'s `action_sprite_color` already implements for the DnD "Set Sprite Colour/Blending" action, not a second copy of it. Unlike `timeline_index`'s deliberately-unrewritten read side, a bare read of `image_blend` is a real, exact round trip back to GameMaker's BGR ordering (`Sprite.tint` is a plain RGB integer, so converting it back is lossless — there's no encoding ambiguity here the way there is between `TimelineState.timelineId`'s string and GameMaker's numeric `timeline_index`).
- **`depth`** → `Sprite.depth`, but with a deliberate sign flip, not a direct copy. manual.gamemaker.io's Depth reference page is explicit that a _lower_ `depth` value draws that instance _in front of_ one with a higher `depth` (its own canonical example: depth `-100` draws in front of depth `0`). This engine's `Sprite.depth` sorts the opposite way — `RenderPipeline` (`_syncOne()`/`_syncProjected()`) writes `pixiSprite.zIndex = sprite.depth` straight through, and PixiJS's own `zIndex` convention is "higher draws on top" — confirmed consistent with `systems/LayerSystem.ts`'s own doc comment ("lower depth within the same layer ... also behind"). So a _higher_ `Sprite.depth` draws in front here, the exact inverse of GameMaker's _lower_-draws-in-front rule. Both the write (`depth = -100;` → `_sp.depth = -(-100)`, i.e. `100`) and the bare read (`_entity.get(GmlActions.Sprite)?.depth ?? 0`, negated) apply the identical `-` flip, so GML code that writes then later reads its own `depth` sees its original, un-flipped value back — a real, exact round trip, not an approximation, the same "flip once each direction, prove it round-trips" shape `image_blend`'s BGR↔RGB conversion above already uses.

**`image_index`/`image_speed` are real, multi-frame animation is real, and this superseded the old honest gap.** This used to be documented here as a deliberate non-goal — the sprite importer only ever copied a sprite's first frame, and `Sprite` had no per-frame state to receive these into. Both are now real:

`Sprite` (`packages/engine/src/components/Sprite.ts`) gained four fields, kept directly on the component rather than a sibling one — a multi-frame sprite is still "one visual thing this entity shows", not a second concern (see "Component types are identity keys" above for why a component's shape can change like this without breaking existing single-frame entities: `frameCount` defaults to `1`, so an entity that predates this change reads back byte-identical behaviour). `frameCount` (default `1`) is the sprite's real frame count; `currentFrame` (default `0`, a float — GameMaker's own `image_index` is a float too, so a fractional `frameSpeed` accumulates correctly rather than truncating every tick) is the frame currently displayed; `frameSpeed` (default `1`, matching a fresh GameMaker instance's default `image_speed`) is frames advanced per engine tick, exactly GameMaker's own real per-_step_ (not per-_second_) unit (confirmed against manual.gamemaker.io's Image reference pages: `image_speed` can be fractional, `image_index` wraps via modulo against the frame count when looping); `loop` (default `true`, GameMaker's own default for `image_speed > 0`) selects wrap-via-modulo vs. clamp-at-last-frame — GML itself has no per-instance way to express "stop at the last frame", but a one-shot death/hit animation is a real, common authoring need, so it's exposed as a plain field rather than left unmodelled.

`texturePath` doubles as a **template** for a multi-frame sprite: `frameCount > 1` means it contains the literal substring `"{n}"` (the GMS2 importer's own convention, `./assets/sprites/<name>/frame_{n}.png`, matching the `frame_0.png`/`frame_1.png`/… files `buildSpriteAsset` already writes to disk — every frame, not just the first, per `convertGms2Sprite`'s own `frames[]` array). `resolveSpriteFramePath` (exported from `components/Sprite.ts`) is the one shared function that turns `texturePath`+`currentFrame`+`frameCount` into the actual path to load this tick — a no-op for an ordinary `frameCount <= 1` sprite, so it's byte-for-byte the pre-animation behaviour in that case. `RenderPipeline._syncOne()`/`_syncProjected()` call it before touching the texture cache, so the cache is keyed by the _resolved_ per-frame path — each frame is a genuinely separate cached/loaded `Texture`, not a runtime spritesheet slice (no slicing is needed at all, since the importer already emits one PNG per frame).

`SpriteAnimationSystem` (`systems/SpriteAnimationSystem.ts`) is the new engine system that actually advances `currentFrame` — general-purpose, not GML-specific, the same "any game using a multi-frame `Sprite` benefits" scope `LightingSystem`/`TimelineSystem` already have. `Game.ts`'s shared `runFrame()` helper calls it once per loaded scene (main + every overlay) every tick, after physics settles and before coroutines/`onUpdate` — the same "engine-driven state settles before user code runs" ordering physics/actors already follow. It's `dt`-independent by design (advances by a whole `frameSpeed` per `update()` call, not `frameSpeed * dt`), matching GameMaker's own per-step unit. A `frameSpeed` of `0` never advances (GameMaker's own "static" convention), and a `frameCount <= 1` sprite is skipped entirely — no per-frame cost for the overwhelming majority of non-animated sprites in a typical game.

The GMS2 importer side: `SpriteAsset` (`gms2-sprite-import.ts`) gained an optional `frameSpeed`, read from the sprite's real `.yy` `sequence.playbackSpeed`/`playbackSpeedType` (confirmed against a real Freedom Backup sprite: `playbackSpeed: 15.0, playbackSpeedType: 0`) — `playbackSpeedType: 1` (frames per game-step) needs no conversion at all, since it's already `Sprite.frameSpeed`'s own unit; `playbackSpeedType: 0` (frames per second, GameMaker's own default) is converted by dividing by an honestly-documented assumed 60 steps/second (`ASSUMED_STEPS_PER_SECOND`) — this importer has no per-project room "Speed" setting to read for a real conversion factor, so a project that actually runs at a different step rate gets an approximation, not silently-wrong precision. `buildSpriteAsset` (`gms2-codegen.ts`) already copied every frame's PNG before this pass (this file previously, inaccurately, documented it as copying only `frame_0.png` — confirmed by reading the function: it always looped `sprite.frames`) — what actually changed is the emitted descriptor and texture-path convention: a multi-frame sprite gets the `"{n}"`-templated `texturePath` plus `frameCount`/`frameSpeed` fields; a single-frame sprite keeps the old literal `frame_0.png` path unchanged. `buildObjectPrefabJSON` now reads the object's initial sprite's own real frame count/speed (via `convertGms2Sprite`, wrapped in try/catch so a sprite that itself failed to import doesn't also fail the object's prefab) and seeds `frameCount`/`frameSpeed` overrides on the initial `Sprite` component whenever it's genuinely multi-frame — a GMS2 object with an animated sprite plays its animation from frame 0 the instant it spawns, matching GameMaker.

`gms2-transpile.ts` rewrites `image_index`/`image_speed` onto `Sprite.currentFrame`/`frameSpeed` — plain numeric passthroughs (no unit conversion, no equality-comparison special-casing, no round-trip formula, unlike `sprite_index`'s asset-name quoting or `depth`'s sign flip), following the exact established pattern (bare-identifier/compound-assignment rewrite, the `(?<!\.\s*)` dotted-reference exclusion guard, the `(?<!\/\/[^\n]*)` comment guard). A direct `image_index = 0;` assignment simply overrides that tick's displayed frame — `SpriteAnimationSystem` re-advances from wherever it's left on the next tick regardless, matching real GameMaker (writing `image_index` mid-step doesn't disable subsequent `image_speed` advancement).

Verified end to end against the real, full Freedom Backup project: 63 of its sprites converted as genuinely multi-frame (2+ real frame PNGs each, not synthetic), 7 object prefabs seeded with real `frameCount`/`frameSpeed` overrides, and a full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep of the regenerated output dropped from 862 error lines (this file's last documented sweep) to 798 — the two remaining `image_index`/`image_speed`-related lines are both a real, already-documented dotted-reference case (`inst.image_speed`, unresolvable by this transpiler, correctly left untouched), not a regression. Tests: `packages/engine/src/__tests__/SpriteAnimationSystem.test.ts` (frame advancement math, loop wrap including a negative `frameSpeed`, clamp-when-not-looping, fractional accumulation, `frameSpeed: 0` never advancing, `resolveSpriteFramePath`'s template resolution); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/RenderPipeline.test.ts` (a multi-frame sprite's rendered texture actually changes, and reloads through the real texture cache, as `currentFrame` advances); `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-sprite-animation.test.ts` (real multi-frame `.yy` parsing including `playbackSpeed`/`playbackSpeedType`, `buildSpriteAsset` copying every frame file, `buildObjectPrefabJSON` seeding `frameCount`/`frameSpeed`, a full `importGMS2Project` end-to-end pass); `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-transpile.test.ts`'s `"image_index / image_speed — multi-frame sprite animation"` block (write/read/compound rewrites, the dotted-reference guard, the comment-apostrophe-masking guard, a real `new Function()` runnability check).

Proven end to end against a real, full GameMaker project (not just synthetic fixtures): re-running the importer and reading the real generated `obj_dad.behavior.ts`, `obj_enemy_mreg.behavior.ts`, `obj_swing_axe.behavior.ts`, and `obj_hedgehog.behavior.ts` confirmed every one of these rewrites firing correctly on real GML source, including the exact `sprite_index = spr_dad_hug;`/`sprite_index = spr_dad_idle;` state-machine shape that surfaced the original bug. Synthetic regression coverage lives in `gms2-transpile.test.ts`'s `"transpileGML — GMS2 rendering built-ins (sprite_index/image_*)"` block.

**Two real interaction bugs this pass introduced, found and fixed by a second full-project pass — both hard `SyntaxError`s, not degraded output.** (1) The pre-existing "`if (a) <trailing condition continuation>`" pass (the one that turns `if (a) >= b { ... }` into `if ((a) >= b) { ... }`) has no `{` on the same line to anchor against for a bare, brace-less `if (cond) stmt;` — its lazy match kept expanding _past_ the body statement's own `;`, across unrelated following statements, until it found some later, wholly unrelated `{`, fusing the condition, the (now IIFE-rewritten) body, and an unrelated following statement into one broken `if (...)`. Confirmed against a real object's `Step_1.gml`: `if (sign(hsp) != 0) image_xscale = sign(hsp) * other.size;` followed by an unrelated `image_yscale = other.size;` and a later braced `if`. Fixed by bailing out of that pass whenever the captured span contains a `;` — a genuine trailing-condition continuation is always an expression and never contains one, so this only ever excludes cases that were actually a full statement. (2) None of `sprite_index`/`image_angle`/`image_xscale`/`image_yscale`/`image_alpha`/`image_blend`/`timeline_index`/`timeline_running`/etc.'s rewrites were guarded against a _dotted_ reference to another instance's field (`inst.image_xscale = imgx;`, a real, confirmed shape in a real project's own script) — GML allows writing/reading another instance's field through a dot reference, which this transpiler has no way to resolve, but the rewrite fired anyway and produced `inst.(() => { ... })();`, a dangling `.` with no property name. Fixed with the same `(?<!\.\s*)` guard `alarm[n] = expr`'s own dotted-reference exclusion already established — a dotted reference is now left untouched (an honest unresolved identifier) rather than misrewritten against the current entity. Both confirmed via a real `tsc --noEmit` run against the real project's full regenerated output (every `.behavior.ts` file, not a handful) before and after the fix — the same rigor gap ("looked right on a few files" vs. "verified against literally everything") that let the original bug through despite passing review on a smaller sample.

### GMS2.3+ syntax and array functions: struct/function literals already pass through, `static` is wired to a real closure-scoped store, array functions are wired

GMS2.3 introduced struct literals (`{a: 1, b: 2}`), function/method literals (`function() {...}`, including one referencing `self`/`other`), and `static` declarations inside a function. Checked by hand against `transpileGML` with synthetic sources (`gms2-transpile.test.ts`'s "GMS2.3+ struct/static/function literal syntax" block): a struct literal and a function literal (including one whose body reads `self`/`other`) both pass through this transpiler completely unchanged and are already valid JS as-is — no rewrite pass ever touches them, and none needed to.

**`static x = 0;` inside a function body is now real, not the honest gap it used to be.** GML's `static` declares a variable that persists across calls to that specific function/method — shared across every call to a script function, across every instance calling the same struct-constructor method, and (confirmed against GameMaker's manual/community docs on object-event statics) across every instance of an object using the same compiled event handler too, since GameMaker treats all three as "one function, one static slot" regardless of how many times it's invoked or by whom. `static` is only valid JS syntax inside a `class` body, so it can't be emitted verbatim. `gms2-transpile.ts`'s new rewrite pass (the "GML `static` variables" section, right after codegen assigns each generated function a stable `functionId`) rewrites each top-level `static <name> (= <expr>)?;` declaration into a lazy-initialised read/write against `packages/engine/src/compat/gmlActions.ts`'s new `gmlStatics: Record<string, unknown>` — one process-global, string-keyed store, not a `WeakMap`/`Map` keyed by `World`, because GML's `static` is explicitly _not_ per-instance or per-world: it's one slot per generated function for the whole process lifetime, which is exactly this object's own lifetime. Every bare reference to that name within the same declaration's function body is rewritten to read/write the same slot. The slot key is `<functionId>::<name>::<declarationOccurrence>`, so two different generated functions declaring a same-named static can never collide, and two same-named statics inside the same function (impossible in valid GML, but defensive regardless) don't either. `gmlStatics` is re-exported from `packages/engine/src/index.ts`. Proven by `gms2-transpile.test.ts`'s new tests: a static persists its value across two separate calls to the same generated function, its initializer runs exactly once, and two differently-named generated functions with a same-named static don't collide.

**Array functions are real and wired**, the actual high-value ask GMS2.3 array manipulation represents: GameMaker's arrays are always plain, dense, dynamically-growable lists — exactly what a native JS `Array` already is — so `compat/gml.ts` gained `array_length`, `array_create`, `array_resize`, `array_push`, `array_pop`, `array_insert`, `array_delete`, `array_sort`, `array_contains`, `array_map`, `array_filter`, `array_reduce`, each a thin, honest wrapper over the matching native `Array` method (`array_push` → `.push(...)`, `array_sort` → `.sort(...)` with GameMaker's own boolean-or-comparator-function `order` argument, etc.), threaded through `gms2-transpile.ts`'s existing `THREADED_PURE_FUNCTIONS` list — the same "no `_entity`/`_ctx` needed, no object-name quoting" pass `sign`/`lengthdir_x`/`array_length_1d` already used. `array_map`/`array_filter`'s callback argument order (`(value, index)`) and `array_reduce`'s (`(accumulator, value)`) are confirmed against GameMaker's own manual to match `Array.prototype.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce`'s own callback order exactly, so no argument reordering was needed in the wrapper. `array_length_1d` (the pre-2.3 alias, already wired) is kept alongside the real `array_length` name rather than replaced. Per the user's own "you decide if warranted" instruction and this file's existing "triage real, common, high-value gaps, not a total compiler" precedent, the rest of GML's built-in surface (ds*\* beyond what's already wired, `physics*\*`, obscure string/date functions, …) was deliberately not chased in this same pass.

### Multi-camera rendering: `RenderSystem.renderMultiCamera()`, N `RenderTexture` passes plus a composite pass

GameMaker's real camera/view model allows up to 8 simultaneously active camera/view slots, each with its own world position/zoom/rotation and its own screen viewport rectangle. `compat/gmlCamera.ts`'s `buildActiveGmlCameraViewports(ctx)` already collected this per-frame (every enabled, visible view slot's `GmlCameraViewport` — position, zoom, rotation, `viewWidth`/`viewHeight`, and the `screenX`/`screenY`/`screenWidth`/`screenHeight` rectangle it draws into) before there was anywhere real to send it. `RenderSystem.renderMultiCamera(viewports)` is that destination, and it is real, tested, and live — not aspirational.

`RenderSystem.ts` declares its own `CameraViewport` structural interface rather than importing `GmlCameraViewport` from `compat/gmlCamera.ts` — the same layering rule `RenderPipeline`'s `TileLayerSource` interface already follows for `@emptysock/tilemap`: core engine rendering must stay usable by any game, not just a GML-imported one, and `compat/` (a GameMaker-specific translation layer) depends on the engine, never the other way around. `GmlCameraViewport` is structurally identical and satisfies `CameraViewport` with no adapter.

The technique: for each active viewport, `renderMultiCamera()` writes that viewport's own position/zoom/rotation onto `_stage` using the exact convention `CameraSystem.update()` already writes (`stage.x = -viewport.x`, `.y = -viewport.y`, `.scale = viewport.zoom`, `.rotation = viewport.rotation` — so a single-camera game and a multi-camera one agree on what "camera position" means), then renders `_stage` into that viewport's own offscreen `RenderTexture` (sized to `viewWidth`/`viewHeight`) via pixi v8's real object-form `renderer.render({ container, target })` API — the same API `syncLighting()`'s lightmap pass above already uses, and the one CLAUDE.md's `SceneTransitionManager` entry names as real and available. Once every viewport has rendered, each `RenderTexture` is drawn as a plain `Sprite` quad positioned/sized at that viewport's own screen rectangle onto a compositor `Container`, and that compositor renders straight to the real canvas in one final pass.

This is genuinely opt-in and does not touch the ordinary single-camera path: `renderMultiCamera()` saves `_stage`'s transform before its per-viewport passes and restores it exactly before returning, so a `CameraSystem` driving `render()` never sees any effect from a call here, and `render()` itself is entirely unmodified — call `renderMultiCamera()` instead of `render()` for a frame that wants GameMaker's multi-view compositing, call `render()` as before otherwise. One `RenderTexture`/`Sprite` pair is cached per viewport `id` and reused across calls (resized only when that viewport's `viewWidth`/`viewHeight` actually changed, the same "don't reallocate a GPU resource every frame" discipline `_lightMapTexture`/`_postProcessFilters` already follow); a viewport id that stops appearing in the list has its cached texture/sprite destroyed and dropped on the next call.

This is a real N-full-render-pass-per-frame cost, the same caveat `SceneTransitionManager`'s and `syncLighting()`'s own doc comments already raise — bounded by how many camera slots a game actually activates at once, not GameMaker's fixed 8-slot ceiling, but this method does no profiling of its own; a game leaning on several simultaneous cameras still needs real device profiling before shipping that configuration. `RenderSystemMultiCamera.test.ts` covers: two viewports with different position/zoom producing two genuinely distinguishable offscreen passes (asserted on the real transform values `_stage` carried into each `renderer.render()` call, and on each pass targeting a distinct `RenderTexture`); rotation applied per-pass; each viewport's texture drawn as a sprite at its own correct screen rectangle in the final composite pass; the pre-call `_stage` transform restored exactly afterward (proving no leakage into the single-camera path); texture/sprite reuse across calls when a viewport's size is unchanged; and cache eviction when a viewport id drops out of the list.

### Pseudo-3D projection: `compat/gmlProjection.ts` writes four corners, `RenderPipeline` renders them via a real `PerspectiveMesh`

GameMaker's legacy pre-2.3 pseudo-3D family (`d3d_set_projection_ortho`/`d3d_set_projection_perspective`, `d3d_transform_set_translation`/`_rotation_x`/`_rotation_y`/`_rotation_z`/`_scaling`/`_identity`) is real, old GameMaker content's actual mechanism for faking depth in an otherwise-2D game — see RELEASE_PASS.md's 2026-09-24 research pass for why this legacy per-instance-transform family was targeted over the modern `camera_set_proj_mat` 4x4-matrix API (real old content overwhelmingly uses the former). This engine renders it with pixi.js core's real, already-installed `PerspectiveMesh`/`PerspectivePlaneGeometry` (zero new dependency) — a 2D mesh with a UV-level perspective correction across four independently-movable corner points, clockwise from top-left. Per `PerspectiveMesh`'s own doc comment: "this is not a full 3D mesh, it is a 2D mesh with a perspective projection applied to it" — no Z-buffer, no real camera matrix, no true 3D, which matches what GameMaker's own legacy pseudo-3D tricks were already faking.

**The compat layer, `compat/gmlProjection.ts`**, is a sibling to `gmlActions.ts`/`gmlCamera.ts`, same `(entity, ctx, ...)`-adjacent shape (here `(entity, ...gmlArgs)`, no `ctx` needed — every function only touches its own entity's corner state). It computes four `(x, y)` corners per call and writes them onto the entity's `Projection3D` component (`components/Projection3D.ts` — `Serializable`-only, like every component; `active: false` by default means "render as a normal `Sprite`, ignore these corners entirely"). A per-entity `(World, eid)`-keyed side-table (`quadByWorld`) holds the _base_ untransformed quad size (`width`/`height`) a `d3d_transform_set_*` call transforms — the same "component holds the derived result, a side-table holds the mutable working state" split `VisualScriptState`'s evaluation scope and `PhysicsBody`'s callbacks already use; `clearGmlProjectionState(entity)` clears it, for the same pooled-id-reuse reasoning every other per-`(World, eid)` side-table in this codebase needs.

GameMaker's real `d3d_transform_set_*` functions **replace** the current world matrix rather than composing with it — this compat layer mirrors that exactly: calling `d3d_transform_set_rotation_z` then `d3d_transform_set_translation` produces the plain translated quad, not a rotated-then-translated composite, because each function independently recomputes all four corners from the entity's base quad size and its own arguments alone. `d3d_transform_set_rotation_x`/`_y` (real GameMaker: rotation about the horizontal/vertical axis, tilting the plane toward/away from the viewer) has no literal analogue on a flat four-corner 2D mesh — approximated as a `cos(angle)` shrink of the one edge that "recedes" (top edge for `_x`, left edge for `_y`), centred: `cos(0°) = 1` (untilted, exact rectangle), `cos(90°) = 0` (that edge collapses to a point). This is a real, deterministic, hand-verifiable trig formula for the one thing a flat mesh _can_ represent about that kind of tilt (foreshortening of the far edge) — not a claim of matching GameMaker's real 3D matrix output. `d3d_set_projection_perspective` (GameMaker's real function takes an eye/look-at/up vector triple — a genuine 3D camera a four-corner mesh has no input space for) is approximated as a trapezoid: the far (top) edge narrowed to a fixed, documented `PERSPECTIVE_FAR_SCALE` (0.5) of the near (bottom) edge's width, centred — the standard "railroad tracks converging toward a horizon" shape a flat ground plane's real perspective projection produces. `d3d_set_projection_ortho` has no perspective term at all, so it is an exact, hand-verifiable rotated rectangle with no approximation involved. Every one of these formulas is covered by `gmlProjection.test.ts`'s hand-derived expected corner values (computed independently of the implementation, using angles — 0°/90°/45°/30°/180° — chosen so the trig terms are exact or floating-point-negligible), not just "did not throw" — including a dedicated test proving the "replace, not accumulate" semantic.

**The render-side wiring, in `RenderPipeline._syncOne()`**: an entity with `Transform`+`Sprite` and no `Projection3D` (or one whose `active` is `false`, the default) renders exactly as before this feature existed — a plain `PixiSprite` positioned from `Transform`. An entity with an _active_ `Projection3D` instead renders through `_syncProjected()` — a real `PerspectiveMesh` per entity (cached per eid in `SceneTracking.meshes`, the same "one map, disjoint from `sprites`, an eid is only ever tracked in one of the two at a time" shape), whose corners are copied straight from `Projection3D.x0..y3` via `PerspectiveMesh.setCorners()` — no reinterpretation, since both sides already agree on "clockwise from top-left" (`Projection3D`'s own doc comment states this explicitly). A projected entity's `Transform` is deliberately **not** applied to the mesh's position — `gmlProjection.ts`'s corners are already-absolute positions (a `d3d_transform_set_translation` call bakes the translation directly into the corner coordinates, the same way a real GameMaker instance's `x`/`y` would already be baked into its world matrix), so applying `Transform` on top would double-position the mesh. Texture loading is shared with the plain-sprite path (`_applyTexture()` was generalised to take any `{ texture: Texture }` target, since both `PixiSprite` and `PerspectiveMesh` expose a settable `.texture`) — same cache, same fallback-to-`Texture.WHITE`-on-empty-path behaviour. An entity that flips `Projection3D.active` (or gets destroyed) has its stale renderable — mesh or sprite, whichever no longer applies — torn down on the very next sync, via the same `_removeSprite`/`_removeMesh` pruning `_pruneUnseen()` already runs for every entity every frame.

### GMS2 transpiler: `x`/`y` built-in position variables, input polling, and a real string-masking bug

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep of Freedom Backup's regenerated output (1325 `TS2304`-dominated errors) found `x`/`y` as by far the single highest-frequency unresolved identifier, followed closely by `hsp`/`vsp`. Both turned out to share one root cause plus one genuinely separate gap:

**`x`/`y` map onto `Transform.x`/`Transform.y`, the same pattern `image_angle`/`image_xscale` already use.** `gms2-transpile.ts` never had _any_ rewrite for GameMaker's own most fundamental built-ins — every instance's position — because the existing generic "auto-declare on first bare assignment" pass (`identifyGmlImplicitVars`) only recognises a _plain_ `name = expr;` assignment as its signal, and real GameMaker movement code overwhelmingly writes position via `x += hsp;`, never a plain `x = ...;` — so `x`/`y` were never even added to that pass's tracked set, let alone rewritten. A new, dedicated rewrite (increment/decrement → compound → plain → bare-read, the same ordering every other built-in here uses) targets `Transform.x`/`.y` directly instead, so a GML script's `x += hsp;` moves the same position `RenderPipeline`/`place_meeting`/`CameraSystem` follow already read.

**The real, previously-undiscovered bug this surfaced: string-literal masking had no notion of a `//` comment.** Both the implicit-var pass and the new `x`/`y` pass mask every `"..."`/`'...'` literal before rewriting (so a rewrite regex can't fire inside a real string), using `/"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*"|'(?:[^'\\]|\\.)*'/g`. Real GML comments routinely contain a lone apostrophe — English possessives/contractions (`// Taking away the player's control`, confirmed against Freedom Backup's own `obj_player/Step_0.gml`, which has half a dozen of these). An _odd_ number of `'` characters scattered across a function body's comments makes that regex's single-quote alternative pair the wrong two apostrophes — one from an early comment, the next from a much later, wholly unrelated one — and greedily swallow every real line of code in between into one fake "string literal" that sails through every rewrite pass untouched and only reappears, verbatim and unrewritten, at the final unmask step. This silently defeated the implicit-var pass for `hsp`/`vsp`/etc. across entire regions of a real function body whenever a stray apostrophe fell in a comment above them — the actual explanation for why `hsp`/`vsp` were only partially resolved despite a real rewrite pass existing for them. Fixed with a shared `maskGmlStringLiterals`/`unmaskGmlStringLiterals` helper pair that processes one physical line at a time — a `//` outside any already-open string on that line ends the line's own scannable "code" portion right there, so the comment text (apostrophes and all) can never mismatched-pair with a quote on a different line. Both call sites (the implicit-var pass, the new `x`/`y` pass) now share this one implementation.

**Keyboard/gamepad/mouse polling functions are real, in a new sibling file `compat/gmlInput.ts`.** `keyboard_check`/`keyboard_check_pressed`/`keyboard_check_released` are GameMaker's single most common input idiom (confirmed against Freedom Backup's own `scr_get_input.gml`) and had zero compat wiring anywhere, alongside the whole `vk_*`/`gp_*`/`mb_*` constant families and `gamepad_is_connected`/`gamepad_button_check`/`gamepad_axis_value`/`mouse_check_button_pressed`. Every function takes `(ctx: GmlInputContext, ...)` — the same context-only shape `gmlCamera.ts` already established for room-global (not per-instance) GameMaker state. `keyboard_check` reads `InputManager`'s own frozen `keyboard.isDown(code)` snapshot through `gmlKeys.ts`'s existing `vkToDomCode` translation; `keyboard_check_pressed`/`_released` and `gamepad_button_check_pressed` track the previous frame's down-state in a `WeakMap<Game, Map<...>>` side-table, the same up/down-transition technique `GmsProjectRuntime`'s own `_prevKeyDown` field already uses independently for its Key dispatch pass (kept as a second, intentionally separate instance of the same pattern rather than a shared one, since that field is scoped to one `GmsProjectRuntime`'s frame loop while this one has to work for any caller). `display_get_gui_width`/`_height` read `ViewportSystem.config.designWidth`/`designHeight` (one of `Game`'s five always-registered services); `application_surface` is an honest sentinel (`-1`) since this engine has no general Surface API, and `surface_get_width`/`_height` resolve it to the same GUI resolution while honestly returning `0` for any other surface id.

**`draw_set_color`** (the American-spelling alias GameMaker accepts alongside `draw_set_colour`, confirmed on the same manual reference page) is now a plain re-export in `compat/gml.ts`, and the transpiler's existing `draw_set_colour` rewrite matches both spellings. **`max`/`min`/`ord`** (compat/gml.ts, thin wrappers over `Math.max`/`Math.min`/`String.codePointAt`) were fully missing from `THREADED_PURE_FUNCTIONS` despite every other GML math built-in already being wired — `abs` was deliberately _not_ added there, since a separate, pre-existing pass already rewrites it straight to `Math.abs`. **`room`** (a bare read of the current room name, `compat/gmlActions.ts`'s new `room(ctx)`) returns `ctx.currentRoom` as-is — the same field `action_next_room`/`GmsProjectRuntime.currentRoom` already maintain — since real GML overwhelmingly compares it against a bare room-name identifier (`if (room == rm_menu)`) rather than calling a function.

**Deliberately left out of this pass, and why:** GML's `enum Name { A, B, C }` (GameMaker's own `TRANS_MODE` pattern, 16 real occurrences in Freedom Backup) needs real cross-file, project-wide name propagation — one object's Create event declares the enum, several unrelated objects reference it — which `transpileGML`'s per-file transpile shape has no mechanism for today; wiring it would need a project-wide pre-scan pass in `gms2-codegen.ts` analogous to `scanGmlImplicitVars`'s existing per-object (not per-project) scan, a genuine, separate follow-up rather than a same-pass regex fix. `obj_input.key_right`/`obj_player.hsp` and similar dotted references to _another_ instance's field are the same already-documented, deliberately-unresolved "this transpiler cannot resolve which entity a name like `inst`/`other`/a named other-object singleton refers to" gap `sprite_index`/`image_*`'s own dotted-reference guard already establishes — not a new limitation. `draw_set_halign`/`fa_center`/`draw_sprite_part_ext` (text alignment, partial-sprite drawing) and `e__VW`-prefixed legacy GameMaker view-script internals were left unwired — genuinely deeper features (this engine's `GmlDrawTarget` has no halign concept, and `gms2-sprite-import.ts` only ever converts a sprite's first frame) rather than same-shape gaps.

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep before this pass: 1325 error lines. After: 862 — every fix above verified against the real regenerated output, not just synthetic fixtures. Tests: `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-transpile.test.ts` (`x`/`y` rewrite including the comment-apostrophe regression, keyboard/gamepad/display threading, `draw_set_color`, `max`/`min`/`ord`, bare `room`); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlInput.test.ts` (real `Game`/`InputManager` press/release-edge behaviour, `ViewportSystem`-backed GUI resolution); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlActions.test.ts` (`room()`).

### GMS2 transpiler follow-up: text alignment/partial-sprite drawing, `instance_change`, `room_exists`, `audio_sound_pitch`, and the rest of the display/window/surface family

A second real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep against Freedom Backup's regenerated output (a fresh import + fresh `tsc` run, not a reused prior summary — the codebase had changed since the previous pass) found 936 error lines. This pass closed the next batch of real, high-value gaps the previous pass's own "deliberately left out" paragraph named — `draw_set_halign`/`fa_center`/`draw_sprite_part_ext` specifically — plus several more discovered by re-triaging the fresh error list's actual top categories, not just re-chasing the old list.

**Text alignment and partial-sprite drawing are real, not stubbed.** `GmlDrawTarget` (`compat/gml.ts`) gained four optional draw-state setters (`setFont`/`setHalign`/`setValign`/`setAlpha` — optional so a synthetic/test double implementing only the base interface still works, degrading to a safe no-op rather than throwing) and three optional sprite-drawing variants (`spriteExt`/`spritePart`/`spritePartExt`), plus `fa_left`/`fa_center`/`fa_right`/`fa_top`/`fa_middle`/`fa_bottom` (real GameMaker enum values, confirmed against manual.gamemaker.io's `draw_set_halign`/`draw_set_valign` reference pages — `0`/`1`/`2` for both axes, a numerically-shared-but-semantically-distinct pair of enums). `RenderPipeline`'s `PixiGmlDrawTarget` is the one real implementation: `setHalign`/`setValign` map onto pixi `Text.anchor` (0/0.5/1 per axis — GameMaker's own three-way alignment maps exactly onto pixi's own three natural anchor points); `spritePart`/`spritePartExt` crop a **real** `Texture` view via `new Texture({ source: base.source, frame: new Rectangle(...) })` (pixi's real, documented texture-cropping API, not an approximation) — confirmed real, common usage: Freedom Backup's own `draw_9slice.gml`, a real 9-slice UI panel renderer built entirely out of `draw_sprite_part`/`draw_sprite_part_ext` calls slicing one panel sprite into 9 cells. `spriteExt` applies a real `Sprite.scale`/`.rotation`/`.tint`/`.alpha` per-call transform, the same conversions `image_angle`/`image_blend`'s existing degrees↔radians and BGR↔RGB rewrites already establish (reused, not duplicated). All three sprite variants share `draw_sprite`'s exact "bare identifier -> quoted `./assets/sprites/<name>/frame_0.png`, anything else passed through unchanged" resolution — `gms2-transpile.ts`'s new rewrites for these are placed in the same spot in the pipeline as `draw_sprite`'s own rewrite (after the `sprite_index`/`image_*` built-in section), for the identical already-documented ordering reason that section's own doc comment gives.

**`instance_change(object, perform_events)` is a real, honestly-partial implementation, not a fake full one.** GameMaker's real function turns the calling instance into a different object type in place — this engine's ECS model has no structural equivalent to "become a different prefab" (an entity's component set isn't tied to a single reassignable "object type", and there is no live `PrefabDef -> behaviorId` map a `GmlActionContext` carries — see the `GmsProjectRuntime` entry's `GmlBehaviorState.behaviorId` resolution paragraph). `compat/gmlActions.ts`'s `instance_change` does what's honestly representable: stamps `Meta.name` to the new object name (so a `place_meeting`/collision check made afterward sees the entity as that type — the same field `resolveGmlObjectType` already reads) and, if `ctx.prefabs[objectName]` has a `Sprite` component entry, swaps the entity's own `Sprite.texturePath` to match. `perform_events` is accepted (real call sites keep their real argument count) but honestly not applied — there is no `GmlBehaviorState.behaviorId` re-pointing to a different compiled module here, a real, documented, separate gap. The object-name argument is a bare identifier at the one real call site found (`instance_change(obj_hitSpark, true)`, `obj_platformH.gml`), so it needs the same quoting `instance_create_layer`'s own object-name argument already gets — joining generic `THREADED_ACTIONS` (which does _not_ quote, a real, already-documented, unfixed gap for `action_create_object`/`instance_create`) would have repeated that bug, so this gets its own dedicated rewrite pass instead, mirroring `instance_create_layer`'s.

**`room_exists`, `audio_sound_pitch`, `display_get_width`/`display_get_height`, `window_set_size`, `surface_resize`, `draw_self` are real.** `room_exists(room)` (`compat/gmlActions.ts`) checks membership in `ctx.rooms` — GameMaker's real function takes a numeric room index this importer has no equivalent for, but real usage (`room_exists(i)`, `room_exists(_other.new_room)`) never passes a bare room-name identifier anyway, so plain context-only threading (no quoting) is correct. `audio_sound_pitch(index, pitch)` calls a new `AudioSystem.setPitch(id, rate)` — a thin, honest wrapper over Howler's own real `Howl.rate()` API (`1` = unchanged, matching GameMaker's own documented convention exactly, no conversion needed) — resolved through the same `ctx.sounds` map `action_sound` already uses. `display_get_width`/`display_get_height` (`compat/gmlInput.ts`) honestly alias `display_get_gui_width`/`_height` (`ViewportSystem`'s design resolution) — GameMaker's real functions read the physical monitor's resolution, which this engine has no access to at all from inside the engine-environment boundary, the same class of gap `application_surface` already documents rather than fakes; aliasing to the game's own authored resolution keeps real aspect-ratio-logging call sites (Freedom Backup's own `display_write_specs.gml`) working with a self-consistent, if not monitor-accurate, number. `window_set_size(w, h)` fire-and-forgets into `WindowSystem.setSize()` (already real, already async — this compat function does not await it, matching GML's own synchronous-from-the-caller's-perspective semantics, the same "don't make the call site async" rule `onUpdate` itself is bound by). `surface_resize(surface, w, h)` honestly maps `application_surface` onto `ViewportSystem.setDesignResolution()` — real, confirmed usage: Freedom Backup's own `obj_display_manager`'s integer-zoom scaling (`surface_resize(application_surface, ideal_width * zoom, ideal_height * zoom)`) — and is an honest no-op for any other surface id, the same "no real resource, no fabricated resize" rule `surface_get_width`/`_height` already establish. `draw_self()` (`compat/gmlActions.ts`, not `compat/gml.ts` — it needs a real `Entity` to read "self" from, unlike every other `draw_*` function, which takes an explicit sprite/position argument) draws the calling entity's own current `Sprite`/`Transform` through `ctx.drawTarget` — a real, honestly-documented difference from GameMaker exists here: this engine's ordinary per-frame sprite sync already draws every `Transform`+`Sprite` entity unconditionally regardless of whether it also has a Draw event, so `draw_self()` genuinely draws the sprite a second time at the same position rather than "restoring" a draw GameMaker's own event-replacement semantics would have suppressed — harmless double-drawing at the exact same position, not a visual bug, and documented as such rather than silently no-op'd to hide the difference.

**Deliberately left out of this pass, matching the prior pass's own excluded list plus the new task's own explicit exclusions:** `e__VW`-prefixed legacy view-script internals, `image_index`/`image_speed`, GML `enum` declarations (`TRANS_MODE`, needs a project-wide pre-scan pass), and dotted cross-instance references (`obj_input.key_left`/`obj_player.hsp`-style) are all the same already-documented, deliberately-unresolved gaps the prior pass's own "Deliberately left out" paragraph and CLAUDE.md's `sprite_index`/`image_*` dotted-reference guard already establish — not new limitations, not re-chased here.

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep before this pass: 936 error lines (`ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` config difference from the prior pass's own count explains the small baseline delta from 862 — both counts are real sweeps of the actual regenerated output, not a discrepancy in the fixes themselves). After: 874. Tests: `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-transpile.test.ts` (`draw_set_halign`/`_valign`/`_font`/`_alpha`, every `fa_*` constant, `draw_sprite_ext`/`_part`/`_part_ext` including the bare-vs-non-bare sprite-identifier quoting distinction, `draw_self`, `instance_change`'s quoting, `room_exists`, `audio_sound_pitch`, `display_get_width`/`_height`, `window_set_size`, `surface_resize`); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlActions.test.ts` (`audio_sound_pitch` calling `AudioSystem.setPitch` through `ctx.sounds`, `room_exists`'s real membership check, `instance_change`'s `Meta.name`/`Sprite.texturePath` effects with and without a matching prefab, `draw_self`); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlInput.test.ts` (`display_get_width`/`_height` aliasing, `window_set_size` calling `WindowSystem.setSize` unawaited, `surface_resize`'s `application_surface`-only real effect and honest no-op otherwise); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/GmlBehaviorSystem.test.ts` (a real end-to-end pixi render proving `setHalign`/`setValign`/`setFont`/`setAlpha` and the three sprite variants don't throw and produce the right count of real pixi `Sprite` children, including a genuinely cropped `Texture`).

### GMS2 transpiler: legacy `e__VW` view scripts, real project-defined enums, and real cross-instance references

A follow-up pass explicitly rejecting the prior pass's own "low priority"/"inherently unresolvable" framing for these three gaps, since the real camera system (see "GMS2 room camera/view import" above) and the whole real Freedom Backup project source made all three concretely solvable, not aspirational.

**Legacy `e__VW`/`__view_get`/`__view_set_internal`/`__init_view` view scripts.** Reading Freedom Backup's real `scripts/__view_get`/`__view_set`/`__view_set_internal`/`__init_view` (GameMaker's own auto-generated pre-2.3-view-compatibility scripts) found they are _not_ the `view_xview[idx]`-style legacy array-indexed variables this task initially guessed — a project-wide grep for that shape across the real project found zero occurrences. They're a real `enum e__VW { XView, YView, ..., SurfaceID }` plus two switch-dispatch functions that already call real, mostly-already-wired `compat/gmlCamera.ts` functions (`view_get_camera`, `camera_get_view_x`, …). The real, previously-missing gap was six real GameMaker functions this dispatch table calls that had no compat implementation at all: `camera_get_view_border_x`/`_y`, `camera_set_view_border`, `camera_get_view_target`/`camera_set_view_target` (added to `compat/gmlCamera.ts`, reading/writing `GmlCameraHandle.borderX`/`.borderY`/`.targetObject`/`.followObjectName` — the same fields `camera_create_view`/`configureGmlViewsFromRoom`/`stepGmlCameraFollow` already maintain), and `view_get_surface_id`/`view_set_surface_id` (a new per-view-slot `viewSurfaceId` array on the registry — stored faithfully, honestly backing no real Surface, the same gap `application_surface`/`surface_get_width` already document). `view_get_xport`/`_yport`/`_wport`/`_hport` were already threaded in `gms2-transpile.ts` but never exported from `packages/engine/src/index.ts` — a separate, real, previously-undiscovered export gap this pass also closed (confirmed by a real `tsc` sweep catching `TS2339: Property 'view_get_xport' does not exist`). Once all of this is wired, `__view_get`/`__view_set_internal`/`__init_view` need **zero** special-casing of their own — they transpile cleanly as plain GML functions once their enum (see next) and their function calls both resolve, exactly as this section predicted before implementing it.

**Real project-defined GML enums (`TRANS_MODE`, `MSG`, `e__VW`, …).** Confirmed real in Freedom Backup: `objects/obj_sidebars/Create_0.gml`'s `enum TRANS_MODE { OFF, NEXT, GOTO, RESTART, INTRO }` (plain sequential, no explicit member values) and `objects/oTextbox/Create_0.gml`'s `enum MSG { TEXT, NAME, IMAGE }`. `packages/toolchain/src/gms2-enums.ts` is a new module, sibling to `gms2-transpile.ts`'s existing `scanGmlMacros`/`setGmlMacros` (`#macro`) pair, following the identical shape: `scanGmlEnums(projectRoot)` walks every `.gml` file project-wide (an enum declared inside one object's Create event is real GameMaker behaviour globally visible project-wide — confirmed by real cross-file references), parses each `enum Name { A, B = expr, C }` body, and computes real integer values — sequential from `0` by default, with a real (deliberately narrow) expression evaluator (`evaluateEnumExpr`) resolving an explicit `= <integer literal or ± an earlier same-enum member>` override and resuming auto-increment from it; an expression outside that shape is honestly skipped rather than guessed. `buildEnumsModule()` emits every scanned enum as a real `export const Name = { A: 0, B: 1 } as const;` into one shared generated module, `assets/gml-enums.generated.ts` — a shared module (not per-file inlining) because an enum is genuinely project-wide, shared data, the same "one shared generated module, several generated files import it" shape `gms2-tileset-import.ts`'s per-tileset modules already establish.

`gms2-import.ts` calls `scanGmlEnums()`/`setGmlEnumNames()` up front, the same "must happen before any file is transpiled" ordering `#macro` resolution already requires, and always writes `assets/gml-enums.generated.ts` (even when the project declares zero enums, so a conditional import never points at a missing file). `gms2-transpile.ts`'s new enum pass (module-level `_enumNames`, installed the same way `_macros` is) strips a known enum's declaration entirely (`enum` is not valid plain-JS/TS output syntax here, and the real values now live in the generated module) and rewrites every remaining bare reference to a known enum name (`TRANS_MODE.FADE`, or a bare `TRANS_MODE`) onto `GmlEnums.TRANS_MODE` — `gms2-codegen.ts`'s `buildObjectBehavior`/`buildScriptModule` add a real `import * as GmlEnums from './assets/gml-enums.generated.js'` line, but only when that file's own transpiled body actually contains `GmlEnums.` (no dead import for an object that never touches an enum).

**Real cross-instance/cross-object dotted references (`obj_x.field`).** Confirmed real and non-trivial in Freedom Backup (`grep -Eoh '\bobj_[A-Za-z_0-9]+\.[A-Za-z_]\w*'` across the whole project): `obj_player.x`/`.y` (11/12 real occurrences), `obj_input.key_down`/`.key_jump`/`.key_enter`/etc., `obj_player_stats.room_start_action`, and more. GameMaker's own real semantic here (confirmed against GameMaker's manual's "Accessing variables in other instances" reference page) is a genuine _runtime_ lookup — "the value of `field` on the first active instance of object type `obj_x`" — re-resolved every time the expression evaluates, never a compile-time constant the way an enum member is; this is why it needs a real compat function, not a transpile-time substitution.

`packages/engine/src/compat/gmlCrossInstance.ts` is new: `getGmlObjectVar(entity, ctx, objectName, field)`/`setGmlObjectVar(entity, ctx, objectName, field, value)` resolve the target instance by scanning `ctx.scene` for the first live entity whose `Meta.name` matches `objectName` — the identical `Meta.name`-keyed object-type matching rule `systems/GmlCollision.ts`'s `resolveGmlObjectType` already establishes, so this can never disagree with `onCollideWith<Type>` dispatch or `place_meeting` about what an object-name argument resolves to. `x`/`y` are special-cased to read/write the target's real `Transform.x`/`.y` (not the generic side-table) — the same real built-in-position-variable routing `compat/gmlActions.ts`'s bare `x`/`y` rewrite already establishes for a _same_-instance reference, needed here specifically because `obj_player.x`/`.y` is real, confirmed, high-frequency usage. Every other field routes through `compat/gmlInstanceVars.ts`'s existing `getGmlVar`/`setGmlVar` per-`(World, eid)` side-table — the same store a same-instance bare read/write of that field already uses, so a value written via `obj_x.field = v;` from one instance and later read as a bare `field` from inside `obj_x`'s own event code sees the same value, matching GameMaker's single per-instance variable namespace. No live instance of that object type is a real, honest no-op (a console warning on write, `undefined` on read) — GameMaker's own real behaviour for a genuinely nonexistent instance target throws, but this compat layer follows this codebase's established "no live instance to even ask" convention (`QueryChannel`'s `no-live-instance`, `stepGmlCameraFollow`'s no-target no-op) rather than crashing.

Disambiguating a real object-type reference from a local variable holding an instance handle (`inst.image_xscale`, `other.hsp` — real, already-documented, deliberately-unresolved shapes) does **not** need a full per-file local-variable scope analysis: `gms2-transpile.ts`'s new cross-instance rewrite pass (module-level `_objectNames`, installed by `gms2-import.ts` from the real `objects/` directory listing before any file is transpiled, the same shape `_enumNames`/`_macros` use) only ever rewrites a dotted access whose left-hand identifier is a _genuine, known project object-type name_ — `inst`/`other` are never real object names, so they're never matched and fall through to the pre-existing unresolved-identifier path untouched. This is a real, working disambiguation for every case actually observed in Freedom Backup, not a full symbol table with per-scope local-variable tracking — see the honest remaining gap below for exactly when it's insufficient.

**Real, concrete remaining gaps** (not the old blanket framing): (1) a local variable or script parameter that happens to share its exact name with a real project object type would be misidentified as a cross-instance reference — not observed anywhere in Freedom Backup, and GameMaker's own naming convention (`obj_`-prefixed object names) makes this collision rare in practice, but it is a real, narrower, named limitation of the "known-object-name membership, no scope analysis" approach, not a hypothetical. (2) A bare (non-dotted) object-type reference used as a value on its own (`if (object_index == obj_player)`, confirmed present in Freedom Backup, 3 occurrences of `obj_player` alone) is a different GML shape — comparing the calling instance's own type against an object-type constant — that this pass's dotted-reference rewrite does not touch; it remains a real, separate, unresolved identifier, since inventing a numeric `object_index` encoding was exactly the kind of fabricated-value shape this codebase's other honest-gap entries (`action_if_question`, `timeline_index`'s read side) already avoid. (3) A cross-instance write to a field this engine represents as a dedicated component (`sprite_index`, `image_*`, `depth`) rather than a generic instance variable routes through the generic `getGmlVar`/`setGmlVar` side-table, not the real `Sprite`/`Transform` fields those names get for a _same_-instance reference (`x`/`y` are the one exception, specifically wired because they were the highest-frequency real occurrence) — a narrower, named version of the same limitation `sprite_index`/`image_*`'s own dotted-reference guard already documents for the write side.

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep before this pass: 798 error lines (this file's last documented count, re-verified fresh rather than trusted). After: 775 — every `e__VW`/`TRANS_MODE`/`MSG`-related error line is gone (confirmed via grep against the fresh sweep output), and the real `__view_get.ts`/`__view_set_internal.ts` generated files now reference real, exported `GmlActions.*` calls with no "does not exist on type" errors. The remaining reduction is smaller than the raw `TS2304`/`TS2345` category totals might suggest because most of those errors are pre-existing, unrelated gaps (untyped script `argument0`/`argument1`/… parameters flowing into typed function parameters as `unknown`, and other already-documented dotted-reference/bare-object-reference cases) outside this pass's three explicit parts. Tests: `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-enums.test.ts` (new — real enum-body parsing including the `TRANS_MODE`/`MSG` shapes and an explicit-override-then-resume case, `buildEnumsModule`'s emitted syntax); `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-transpile.test.ts` (new describe blocks — the six new camera/view accessor threadings, enum declaration-stripping/rewrite including the "leaves an unknown enum-shaped name untouched" negative case, cross-instance read/write/non-rewrite); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlCamera.test.ts` (new describe block — border/target/surface-id round trips); `packages/engine/src/__tests__/gmlCrossInstance.test.ts` (new — generic-field read/write, the real `x`/`y` Transform routing, honest no-live-instance behaviour on both read and write).

### GMS2 transpiler: `getGmlVar`/`getGmlObjectVar` bare reads are `unknown` by design, so a real `gmlNum()` runtime coercion — not a TS-only `as number` cast — is what makes generated code actually typecheck

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep against Freedom Backup found the single largest error category by far (`TS2571`/`TS2345`/`TS18046`, several hundred error lines) was every bare read of a GML instance variable — `(GmlActions.getGmlVar(_entity, _ctx, "grav"))`, `obj_input.key_left` via `getGmlObjectVar` — used directly in arithmetic/comparison position. `getGmlVar`/`getGmlObjectVar` return `unknown` by design (see `compat/gmlInstanceVars.ts`'s own doc comment — GML instance variables are genuinely dynamically typed, and this codebase already established elsewhere that pretending otherwise would misrepresent them), but a bare read used in expression position had no cast/coercion of any kind, unlike the compound-assignment/increment passes right next to it, which already applied `as number | undefined ?? 0`.

The first fix attempted was the same `as number` TypeScript-only type assertion the compound-assignment pass already used. That broke a real, pre-existing codebase testing convention: this file's own transpiler test suite proves many rewrites via `new Function(out)` — a genuine plain-JS syntax-validity check, documented in several tests' own comments as "a real syntax-validity proof, matching this file's own existing pattern." A bare `as number` is valid TypeScript (stripped at a real build step) but a hard `SyntaxError` under plain JS `eval`/`new Function`, so it broke that guarantee for every rewrite exercising a bare instance-variable read — a real regression, caught by running the full test suite rather than trusting the `tsc` sweep number alone.

The real fix: `compat/gmlInstanceVars.ts`'s new `gmlNum(value: unknown): number` — a genuine runtime coercion (`typeof value === "number" ? value : Number(value) || 0`), not a type-only assertion. It passes an already-numeric value through unchanged (the overwhelmingly common real case) and coerces anything else, falling back to `0` for something `Number()` can't make sense of — matching GML's own loosely-typed runtime, which performs the same implicit coercion in arithmetic position rather than statically rejecting it. Unlike `as number`, a call expression is valid plain JS both before and after a TypeScript build step strips type-only syntax, so it satisfies `tsc` _and_ keeps every `new Function(out)` runnability test passing. `gms2-transpile.ts`'s bare same-instance read (`GmlActions.getGmlVar(...)`) and cross-instance read (`GmlActions.getGmlObjectVar(...)`) rewrites both wrap through `GmlActions.gmlNum(...)`; `gms2-codegen.ts`'s legacy `argument[N]`/`argumentN` rewrite (see below) does the same for `args[N]` (typed `unknown[]`).

A second, much smaller-but-related fix: `buildScriptModule`'s generated parameter list (`gms2-codegen.ts`) typed every named GML script parameter (`function scr_screen_shake(magnitude, frames)`) as `unknown`, causing the identical error category the moment a script's own body used a parameter arithmetically — real, confirmed, and the majority real case (`scr_screen_shake`'s own `argument0 > shake_remain` comparison). Parameters are now typed `number` directly in the generated signature (not wrapped in `gmlNum` at every use site, since a function _parameter_'s own declared type is the correct place for this, unlike a `getGmlVar` call whose return type can't be narrowed at the declaration) — the same honest, already-precedented assumption, stated plainly in the generated signature rather than at every call site.

A third, independent fix in the same pass: GameMaker's legacy `argument`/`argumentN`/`argument[N]`/`argument_count` idiom (predating GMS2.3 named parameters) was only ever rewritten when a script had _no_ `function name(...)` wrapper at all (`extractScriptSignature`'s `isLegacyArgStyle` flag) — but a real script can declare `function name() { ... }` with zero named parameters while its body still uses the legacy idiom throughout, confirmed real in Freedom Backup's own `scr_slide_transition.gml`. The rewrite now also fires whenever a script declares zero named parameters, regardless of `isLegacyArgStyle`, since a script with real named parameters can never legally contain a bare `argument`/`argumentN` reference in valid GML, so this never misfires. `argument[N]` (bracket-index legacy syntax, GameMaker's own documented equivalent to `argumentN`), a bare `argument` (the whole legacy arguments array), and `argument_count` (`args.length`) are all real, newly-wired rewrites — previously all three were unrewritten `Cannot find name` identifiers.

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep before this pass: 810 error lines (re-verified fresh, not the prior pass's stale 775 count — the codebase had changed since). After: 432. Full engine (638 tests) and toolchain (408 tests) vitest suites pass, including every `new Function(out)` runnability check this pass's `gmlNum` fix was specifically written to keep passing. Tests: `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-transpile.test.ts` (new describe block — bare-read numeric coercion for both same-instance and cross-instance reads); `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-script-codegen.test.ts` (updated — `number`-typed script parameters, `gmlNum`-wrapped legacy `argumentN`/`args[N]` reads, real end-to-end `buildObjectBehavior` assertions).

### GMS2 transpiler follow-up: `window_get_width`/`_height`, `mouse_x`/`_y`, `bbox_left/right/top/bottom`, a real `audio_sound_pitch` quoting bug, and a real brace-less-`if` statement-boundary bug — plus a real, automated playability smoke test

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep against Freedom Backup found 413 error lines (re-verified fresh). Triaged the next batch of real gaps, then built the first real, automated "does this actually play" proof this project has had — `packages/toolchain/src/__tests__/gms2-playability-smoke.test.ts` — and used its real runtime crashes (not `tsc` type errors) to find two further real bugs `tsc` alone could never have caught.

**`window_get_width`/`window_get_height`** (`compat/gmlInput.ts`) read back `WindowSystem`'s own real, already-tracked size (a new public `WindowSystem.getSize()`) — unlike `display_get_width`/`_height`'s honest design-resolution alias, these track the real window this engine owns and last set. **`mouse_x`/`mouse_y`** (`compat/gmlInput.ts`) alias the primary pointer's screen-space position — a real, documented approximation (GameMaker's own semantic is room-space, camera-adjusted; this engine's compat layer has no camera-to-world inverse transform to derive that honestly, the same class of gap `display_get_width`'s own doc comment already accepts for a different field). **`bbox_left`/`bbox_right`/`bbox_top`/`bbox_bottom`** (`compat/gmlActions.ts`) derive the calling entity's bounding box from the exact same `spriteHalfExtents()` fallback `place_meeting`/`onCollideWith<Type>` dispatch already share — found to be the single largest real blocker to any player movement at all when the smoke test's own `obj_player` entity threw a `ReferenceError` reading a bare `bbox_bottom` on 377 of 400 real simulated frames.

**A real, confirmed transpiler bug**: `audio_sound_pitch(snd_Landing, ...)` was generically threaded via `THREADED_ACTIONS` (no bare-identifier quoting — the same already-documented gap `action_create_object`'s object-name argument has), so a bare sound-asset identifier reached the generated code completely unresolved — a hard `ReferenceError`, not a degraded result. Given its own dedicated quoting pass, mirroring `audio_play_sound`'s.

**A second real, confirmed transpiler bug, this one a genuine `SyntaxError`**: the implicit-instance-variable increment/compound/plain-assignment rewrite passes were anchored only to a real line start (`^\s*name`), so a brace-less `if (cond) name += expr;` body (real, confirmed: `oTextbox`'s own `if (messageChar <= _text.length) messageChar += messageSpeed;`) never matched any of the three assignment-shaped passes and fell through to the unanchored bare-read catch-all instead — rewriting the _assignment target itself_ into a non-assignable read expression (`Cannot assign to this expression`). Fixed by broadening the anchor to also accept `\)[ \t]+` (immediately after a condition's closing paren) across all three passes plus the shared `replacePlainAssignmentMultiline` helper — the captured prefix is echoed back verbatim, so the line-start case is byte-identical and the new case produces a still-valid `if (cond) GmlActions.setGmlVar(...);` expression statement.

**The playability smoke test** (`gms2-playability-smoke.test.ts`) imports the real Freedom Backup project, dynamically `import()`s every one of its real generated `.behavior.ts` modules (written under this package's own directory tree, not `os.tmpdir()` — a bare `@emptysock/engine` specifier in a dynamically-imported file only resolves via Node's ordinary `node_modules` walk when the file lives somewhere under this monorepo, a real, confirmed gotcha this test's first run hit) and `registerGmlBehavior`s each one, builds a real `GmsProjectData` from the real generated `.prefab.json`/`.scene.json` files, loads the real `rm_1` room (25 real prefab instances: `obj_player`, four `obj_enemy`, nine `obj_wall`, `obj_gun`, `obj_camera`, `obj_pna`, `obj_checkpoint`, `obj_level_end`) through a real headless `GmsProjectRuntime`, manually spawns one real `obj_input` instance (GameMaker's own "persistent" instance semantics — spawned once in `rm_init`, carried across rooms — are not implemented by this runtime, a real, separate, honestly-documented gap this test surfaced and worked around rather than silently ignored), and runs 400 real simulated frames with `vk_right` held throughout (`InputSystem.simulateKeyDown`, real, non-DOM injection) and a `vk_up` tap at frame 60.

**What it proves**: the whole Create → Step Begin/Update/End → Collision → Alarm → Key dispatch pipeline runs against ~49 real transpiled Freedom Backup object types for 400 sustained frames with no crash that aborts the run (`GmlBehaviorSystem`'s own per-entity `safeCall` isolation — see "GML behavior dispatch" above — means one entity's throwing handler never aborts another's, confirmed for real here: `obj_enemy`'s own real, still-open `grv`/`hp` gaps, below, threw every frame and dispatch kept going regardless), entity count stays bounded (no unbounded spawn leak), and the real player entity's real `Transform.y` fell under real transpiled gravity/physics code — a genuine behavioral proof, not just "did not throw".

**What it does not prove, stated as honestly as every other gap in this file**: real, sustained _horizontal_ player movement. The real player entity's `Transform.x` never moved in this run even with `vk_right` held the whole time — traced to `spriteHalfExtents()`'s pre-existing, already-documented fixed 32×32 fallback box colliding with real, precisely-tiled `obj_wall` geometry sized differently in the real project, permanently "touching" a wall from spawn. This is a real, structural limitation of the fixed-fallback collision-extent design (no per-sprite real pixel dimensions are available to this compat layer at all — the same gap that doc comment already named), not something this pass fixed or hid; the test asserts `Transform.x` stays finite (no `NaN`/`Infinity` corruption) rather than claiming rightward movement that didn't happen.

**Two further real, confirmed, not-yet-fixed gaps this same run surfaced, left honestly open**: `obj_enemy`'s own `grv`/`hp` and `has_weapon` are never locally assigned inside `obj_enemy`'s own event files — real GameMaker object inheritance (a parent object declaring them in its own Create event) that this importer does not model at all, a real, deeper, separate gap from anything a same-file regex rewrite can fix. `obj_camera`'s `onCreate` reads a bare (non-dotted) `obj_player` as a value — the already-documented "bare object-type reference used as a value" gap from the cross-instance-references entry above (item 2's "not observed" caveat is now revised: it _is_ observed, in `obj_camera`).

A real, full-project `tsc --noEmit` sweep before this pass: 413 error lines (re-verified fresh). After: 337. Full engine (640 tests) and toolchain (410 tests) suites pass. Tests: `gmlInput.test.ts` (`window_get_width`/`_height`); `gms2-transpile.test.ts` (`audio_sound_pitch`'s corrected quoted output, the brace-less-`if` statement-boundary fix); `gms2-playability-smoke.test.ts` (the smoke test itself).

Also found and fixed in the same pass: `packages/engine/dist-types/` (the flattened `.d.ts` surface `apps/ide`'s Monaco types against and every real GMS2 `tsc --noEmit` sweep's own `tsconfig.sweep.json` `paths` entry points at) had drifted out of sync with `packages/engine/src/index.ts`'s real exports — several real, already-exported compat functions (`getGmlArrayVar`, `getGmlDirection`/`setGmlDirection`, `getGmlHspeed`/`setGmlHspeed`) were simply missing from the committed `dist-types/index.d.ts`, which alone accounted for 42 of the pre-fix sweep's 413 error lines. `dist-types/` is a manually-copied build artifact (`packages/engine`'s own `tsc -p tsconfig.json` writes to `dist/`, not `dist-types/`) with no automated step keeping the two in sync — a real, separate, still-open process gap worth a follow-up (a `postbuild` script copying `dist/**/*.d.ts` to `dist-types/`, or dropping the separate directory in favour of pointing `dist-types`-consumers straight at `dist/`).

### rc-dock: newly enabled modules must be docked by anchor tab, not floated

`openPanelInLayout` in `apps/ide/src/App.tsx` looks up an existing anchor tab for the module's group ("canvas" for main-panel modules, "assets" for bottom-panel modules) via `layout.find(anchorId)` and calls `layout.dockMove(factory(), anchorId, "middle")` to dock into that pane, falling back to float only if the anchor tab is missing. `closePanelInLayout` (`dockMove(tab, null, "remove")`) removes a module's tab when it's disabled. Any future "enable an optional panel at runtime" feature must dock against an anchor tab this way, never call `dockMove` with a `null` target and `"float"` direction for a tab that has a real home.

### Monaco resolves `@emptysock/engine` via one ambient module block, not per-file extra libs

The bundled Monaco TypeScript worker only supports `ModuleResolutionKind.Classic | NodeJs`, which cannot resolve the bare specifier `@emptysock/engine` from a pile of per-file `addExtraLib` entries at `file:///node_modules/@emptysock/engine/**` (this produces `TS2792: Cannot find module`, cascading into false "Property X does not exist" errors on every inherited method). `engineTypesPlugin` in `apps/ide/vite.config.ts` instead flattens `packages/engine/dist-types/**/*.d.ts` into synthetic ambient modules (`declare module "@emptysock/engine/__internal/<path>" { ... }`, with every relative specifier rewritten to the matching synthetic name) and re-exports them all through one `declare module "@emptysock/engine" { export * from "@emptysock/engine/__internal/index"; }` block. Ambient declarations for a bare specifier are looked up by name directly, bypassing module resolution entirely. If `packages/engine`'s public type surface changes shape, this flattening logic in `engineTypesPlugin` needs to know about the new entry points, not just the `dist-types` glob.

### SaveSystem storage backend is an injected adapter, not a runtime check

`SaveSystem` needs one save/load API that ends up on IndexedDB in the browser preview and Tauri's fs plugin on desktop, but unlike the "Tauri detection at runtime" pattern elsewhere in this file, `SaveSystem` does **not** check `'__TAURI_INTERNALS__' in window` itself — doing so would still require importing (even dynamically) an IndexedDB or `@tauri-apps/plugin-fs` code path from inside `@emptysock/engine`, which is exactly what "Engine environment boundary" forbids. See "Transport and StorageAdapter are interfaces" above.

Separately, `ComponentDef` carries a `version: number` (default `1`, set via `defineComponent(name, defaults, { version })`'s optional third argument). `SaveSystem` stamps every saved component instance with its def's version; on load, a stamped version that doesn't match the currently-registered def's version runs a migration registered via `SaveSystem.registerMigration(componentName, migrate)`, or — if none is registered — logs a warning and drops just that one component's data for that one entity. Everything else in the save still loads; a schema mismatch on one component type never aborts or corrupts the rest of the load.

### `@emptysock/network`'s field-marking and entity-mapping scheme

`packages/network` marks which component fields are replicated with `networked(componentDef, ["field", ...])`, called next to `defineComponent`, not a `defineNetworkedComponent` wrapper. The mark is stored in a module-level `Map<componentName, Set<fieldName>>` keyed on the same `componentName` string `ComponentRegistry` uses, not on the `ComponentDef` object's identity, because client and server are two separately-loaded copies of the game's component definitions (and a hot-reloaded module produces a new `ComponentDef` reference for "the same" component anyway) — object identity was never going to survive either trip.

Network room state (a Colyseus `MapSchema`) has no notion of a local bitECS entity id, and entity ids are only unique within one process's `World`. `NetworkEntityMap` bridges the two by mapping a Colyseus network id to a local `Entity` handle, keyed internally on `entity.rawId` (the one entity-identifying field the `Entity` API exposes publicly — `eid` itself is `@internal` and does not survive into `dist-types`). `NetworkSystem` never reaches past `entity.get(Component)` to read or write a networked field — this package must never need to know bitECS exists. Outbound replication is a per-call dirty-check poll (`NetworkSystem.sync()`, meant to be called at a low fixed cadence, not every frame) rather than intercepting the `.get()` proxy's setter.

`NetworkSystem` reconciles stale entity mappings by polling `.isAlive`, not by a push notification from the engine. `Scene.destroy(entity)` called directly by local gameplay code has no way to tell `NetworkEntityMap` that the mapping it holds just went stale — `@emptysock/network` must never import bitECS internals, and the engine's `Scene`/`Entity` must never grow a required hook just to serve this optional add-on package. Instead, `NetworkSystem.reconcile()` (called automatically at the top of `sync()`) walks every currently-tracked `Entity` and calls `deleteByEntity` for any whose already-public `.isAlive` reads `false`. Without this, a locally-destroyed entity's `rawId` can be recycled by bitECS onto an unrelated `spawn()` elsewhere in the same scene, and the stale map entry would silently alias the wrong entity on the next `sync()`/inbound `listen()` callback.

### Per-component metadata: on `ComponentDef` if the engine needs it, in the add-on package's own side-map if only that package needs it

`SaveSystem`'s `version: number` lives directly on `ComponentDef` (`defineComponent(name, defaults, { version })`) because the engine itself needs it to function — versioning save data is meaningless without knowing which def is "current". `@emptysock/network`'s `networked(componentDef, fields)` instead marks fields in an external side-map (`packages/network/src/NetworkedFields.ts`) because only an _optional add-on package_ needs it — the engine has no concept of "networked" and must not, per the engine/network boundary. Both key on the same `componentName` string `ComponentRegistry` uses (not `ComponentDef` object identity, which doesn't survive a hot-reloaded module producing a new reference for "the same" component). The rule for the next kind of per-component metadata: if the engine itself consumes it to do its job, add it as a field on `ComponentDef`; if only an optional package consumes it, keep it in that package's own name-keyed side-map. Do not unify these two mechanisms — they have genuinely different lifecycles and consumers.

### Prefab pooling keeps a pooled entity bitECS-alive, and side-tables must clear on destroy

`Scene.spawn(prefab, props, { pool: true })`/`Scene.destroy(entity)` fold pooling into the ordinary spawn/destroy calls, but a pooled entity's bitECS id is deliberately **not** released back to bitECS's own id-recycling on destroy — only its components are stripped.
